headline: AFP Deploys Troops, Trucks and Water Assets to Flood-Hit Central Luzon
seoTitle: AFP Deploys Disaster-Response Assets in Central Luzon | FMB News
seoDescription: AFP disaster-response teams are supporting rescue and relief work in Tarlac, Pampanga and Bataan as Habagat flooding continues.
deck: Military disaster-response teams are supporting rescue and relief operations in Tarlac, Pampanga and Bataan as Habagat flooding continues.
author: FMB News Desk

continuation.title: Tropical Storm Pilandok Holds at 65 km/h as Habagat Keeps Seas Rough
continuation.whatChanged: Coverage has moved from the weather threat itself to a documented expansion of military rescue and relief support in flood-hit Central Luzon.

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The Armed Forces of the Philippines said personnel, military vehicles and humanitarian-assistance and disaster-response assets had been deployed to Tarlac, Pampanga and Bataan to support local rescue and relief operations.
AFP spokesperson Col. Francel Margareth Padilla said deployments began on August 29 as flooding worsened in parts of Central Luzon.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The deployment follows days of Habagat-driven flooding while Tropical Storm Pilandok remained offshore. FMB News first covered the broader weather threat on August 31.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Military trucks, boats and trained response teams can add transport and rescue capacity where floodwater has cut road access or stretched local resources.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for additional LGU requests, changes in flood levels, new deployment areas and official reports on evacuations and relief delivery.
